coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 8 units (the domain directory itself plus 7 sub-domain directories containing an *-index.md) and 45 .md files — exactly matching the expected 8 units / 45 files. 03.07 (feature). Every file was read in full, line-numbered, through the 3a implementer-simulation / 3b rubric / 3c devil's-advocate cycle. No sampling. Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity), 4 (Constraint Explicitness), 5 (Success Measurability) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are marked N/A for every unit in this domain: they are owned by meta/problem-statement.md, meta/personas.md, meta/constraints.md and meta/competitive-landscape.md, and every unit here explicitly references rather than redefines them (each Role Matrix carries the rule 'NEVER redefine a persona here — reference only'). Applicable checkpoints per unit are therefore dimensions 3, 7 and 8. The tree is of unusually high quality — most Open Questions tables carry owner + deferral target + blocked-decision, and the [DEEP] files (03.01.01, 03.04.01, 03.06.01, 03.06.04) are close to exemplary. Roughly two thirds of my initial raw candidates were dropped in the 3c pass, chiefly because a cross-reference or a downstream tracked question already carried the detail (e.g. the bare [PENDING] markers in 03.05.02, 03.05.03, 03.08.03 and 03.08.04 all turned out to be covered by a properly-owned Q-row in the same file). The findings that survived are concentrated in two shapes: (a) sub-domain CX files that were never reconciled after a later pass ratified a decision that contradicts them, and (b) inline [PENDING] markers whose deferral target is '/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening' — a stage that has demonstrably already run and closed (03.08.03 Q-04 states this verbatim), leaving those questions with no owner and no live stage to pick them up. I did not read anything under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ other than this run4 output path.

findings.claim: Reachability's degradation behaviour is simultaneously ratified and open: 03.04.01 D-03 decides that all consumers — naming 03.04.04 explicitly — fail CLOSED on a failed traversal, while 03.04.04 carries the same question as a live unresolved Q-04 and its States table records it as undecided.
findings.evidence: 03.04.04-reachability-inbound-policy.md:89 States row — "| Error | Traversal failed | **Fail open or closed?** Failing closed silently drops legitimate contact; failing open lets the flood through on every degradation. Unresolved — Q-04 |" and :129 — "| Q-04 | On traversal failure, does the policy fail open or closed? Closed silently drops legitimate contact; open lets the flood through exactly when the system is already degraded. | Agent | `/create-prd-architecture` |". CONTRADICTED BY 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:225 D-03 — "Traversal failure degrades to **`unknown`**, never to `\"no path\"` | They are different claims... **All consumers fail closed on `unknown`.**"; :169 — "Consumers must fail closed on `unknown`: 03.04.02 must not broker on it, 03.04.04 must not decide reachability on it"; :210 — "Reachability must fail closed on `unknown` (D-03)". Also contradicted by community-networking-cx.md CX-13 synthesis 2 — "If the reachability check is unavailable, results fail *closed* (hidden), never shown-and-broken."
findings.failure_scenario: Two implementers build the reachability evaluator. One reads 03.04.01 D-03 and fails closed, so a degraded graph service silently blocks all unasked inbound contact platform-wide. The other reads 03.04.04 Q-04, sees the decision is deferred to /create-prd-architecture, and picks fail-open as the availability-preserving default — which delivers the full 'check out my beat' flood to every walled Producer during exactly the degradation windows the wall exists to survive. The two builds have opposite behaviour on the same event, and 03.04.04's own Q-04 tells its implementer the question is still theirs to route.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether reachability evaluation fails open or closed when graph traversal returns `unknown`.

findings.claim: 03.06.01 states in two places that scene membership grants no feed-ranking weight and in two other places that membership weights the feed — both citing 03.02.02 by number, with no marker on either.
findings.evidence: 03.06.01-scene-definition-membership.md:21-23 Overview — "**membership is deliberately worthless** (D-08). Joining grants no authority, no ranking weight, no density contribution, and no standing. Everything consequential in this sub-domain — density (03.06.02), stewardship (03.06.03), matching (03.03.02), ranking (03.02.02) — reads **evidence**, never membership." and :232 D-08 — "**Membership grants nothing.** Density, stewardship, ranking and authority all read evidence, never membership". CONTRADICTED BY the same file :123-124 §4 — "So: a scene **is** an addressable place. If a feed exists, membership **also** weights it (03.02.02). Place is required; weighting is an additive optimisation with a dependency." and :174 States — "| Joined (resident) | User accepted an offer or joined by hand | Scene content weights their feed (§4)...". Also :208 Cross-Cut Notes — "scene membership is a ranking axis (DT-03 there)", and community-networking-cx.md CX-03 — "Scene membership is a feed-ranking axis and secondary fan-out set".
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the feed ranker reads D-08 (a numbered, ratified decision in a [DEEP] file) and excludes scene membership from the scoring inputs entirely, so a Bristol user's feed is ranked on follows, geography and evidence only and never surfaces scene-scoped content. A second implementer reads §4 and the Joined (resident) state and adds a membership term to the score. Both cite 03.06.01 and 03.02.02; the resulting feeds differ for every user who has joined a scene, and CX-03's 'scene membership is the feed's secondary fan-out set' is implemented by one and not the other.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether scene membership is an input to feed ranking at all.

findings.claim: The 03.01 CX file still records auto-follow-on-connection-accept as an open convenience the platform MAY implement, while 03.01.01 D-12 and the domain CX R-07 both ratify that it must never happen — a reconciliation 03.01.01 explicitly flagged as required and which never occurred.
findings.evidence: 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements-cx.md:58 CX-02 synthesis 2 — "**Trigger chain**: Accepting a connection MAY auto-create a mutual follow — a convenience most networks implement. If it does, unfollowing later must not silently sever the connection. `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`." CONTRADICTED BY 03.01.01-follows.md:180 D-12 — "**No auto-follow on connection accept** | DT-11. Credit-seeded connections (03.01.02 DT-03) would manufacture follows at scale and inflate the one number DT-06 shows is currency." and community-networking-cx.md R-07 — "Considered auto-following on connection *accept* — the LinkedIn default. Rejected per 03.01.01 DT-11/D-12... Connection and follow stay separate consent acts." 03.01.01-follows.md:152 records the outstanding action verbatim: "DT-11 resolves that CX's open note 2 (no auto-follow on connection accept) from this side — **Step 6 must reconcile the CX file**" — and the domain CX (dated 2026-07-18, Status [DEEP], 'Step 6') ran without reconciling it.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer working the connections sub-domain reads its own CX file's trigger-chain note, implements auto-follow on accept, and adds the unfollow-must-not-sever safeguard it prescribes. Because 03.01.02 DT-03 pre-seeds connections from every verified credit, this manufactures a follow edge for every past collaborator at seed time — inflating the follower count that 03.01.01 DT-06 establishes is booking currency spent in domain 17, which is precisely the outcome D-12 exists to prevent.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether accepting a connection creates a mutual follow edge.

findings.claim: The 03.01 CX file widens endorsement eligibility to include a mutual professional connection as a secondary basis, which the sub-domain decision D-03 and the leaf's own D-01 and edge-case table flatly exclude.
findings.evidence: 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements-cx.md:22-24 CX-01 — "Per D-03, you may only endorse a skill on someone you have a verified collaboration edge with (a confirmed credit from domain 02) **or, secondarily, a mutual professional connection**." CONTRADICTED BY 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements-index.md:59 D-03 — "Endorsement eligibility is **gated by a verified collaboration edge**, not open to anyone... an endorsement from a stranger is noise, and reciprocal endorsement inflation is what made LinkedIn's skill graph worthless", 03.01.03-endorsements-skill-vouching.md:88 D-01 — "Endorsement requires a verified collaboration edge (D-03 on the parent)", and 03.01.03-endorsements-skill-vouching.md:50 edge case — "| No verified collaboration edge exists | Endorsement is not possible | The endorse control is absent...".
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the endorsement authorization check reads CX-01 (the file whose stated scope is precisely the connection↔endorsement interaction) and admits mutual connections as a fallback basis. Because 03.01.02 permits any non-Fan to request a connection and connections are pre-seeded at scale, the anti-inflation gate the whole feature rests on is open: two people who have never shared a session can connect and then endorse each other, which is exactly the LinkedIn failure D-03 cites as its reason for existing. A second implementer reading only the leaf renders no endorse control at all in the same situation.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a mutual professional connection (absent any verified collaboration edge) confers standing to endorse.

findings.claim: 03.06.03's core behaviour — which powers a scene steward actually holds — is entirely unspecified behind a deferral marker pointing at a stage that has already run, and none of its four Open Questions covers it.
findings.evidence: 03.06.03-scene-stewardship-moderation.md:32-33 Behavior — "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — the steward's actual powers are unresolved and are the feature's central question. The plausible range, from weakest to strongest:" followed by a five-row table of candidate powers (curate featured content / welcome arrivals / correct definition or boundary / remove content / remove people) annotated only with risk levels. The file's Open Questions (:107-110) are Q-01 who appoints, Q-02 should Operators steward, Q-03 fan-majority legitimacy, Q-04 unpaid volunteer labour — none asks what the powers are. Only two powers are fixed anywhere: D-02 (:99) "Stewards do not remove people from scenes" and 03.06.01:81-82 ("Splits are proposed by stewards (03.06.03)"). That the deferral target is spent is stated in this domain by 03.08.03-judging-voting-anti-gaming.md:113 — "**Re-pointed**: `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and the `Stalled` state is still `[PENDING]`".
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must build the steward role and finds that only 'cannot remove people' and 'may propose subdivisions' are decided. They must invent whether a steward may remove content from a scene — a High-risk power the file itself flags as 'content moderation by an interested party' — and whether curation of featured content is granted. Grant it and a venue operator can suppress a competing act's activity in their own city's scene, which is the capture failure DT-02 and Q-02 are about; withhold it and stewardship reduces to a welcome message, making D-03's density gate and Q-04's unpaid-labour question meaningless. No stage will pick the question up, because the only marker points at a closed one.
findings.forcedInvention: The steward's granted power set — in particular whether content removal and featured-content curation are in scope.

findings.claim: Roughly two dozen inline `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` markers across the domain defer to a stage that has already run and closed, so each is an open question with no owner and no live stage to resolve it — malformed tracking, not tracked deferral.
findings.evidence: The proof that the target is spent is inside this domain: 03.08.03-judging-voting-anti-gaming.md:113 Q-04 — "**Re-pointed**: `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and the `Stalled` state is still `[PENDING]` in the States table"; likewise 03.08.02:103 — "**Re-pointed**: `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run without answering it". Markers still pointing there include 03.07-forums-craft-qa.md:36 ("voting mechanics, accepted-answer semantics... are unresolved"), 03.10-peer-scene-listening-rooms.md:36, 03.11-conference-event-networking-mode.md:37 ("event sourcing... is unresolved and gates the feature"), 03.06.03-scene-stewardship-moderation.md:32, 03.06.02-scene-graph-density-map.md:36 ("the density metric itself is unresolved"), 03.02.01:45, 03.02.02:40, 03.05.01:41, 03.05.02:40, 03.05.03:37, 03.01.03:37, 03.01-...-cx.md:58 and :67, 03.02-...-cx.md:38, :66, :72, 03.03-...-cx.md:94, 03.04-...-cx.md:94, 03.05-...-cx.md:71, 03.06-...-cx.md:73 and :84. Files that were remediated re-pointed correctly (03.09:82 uses `[PENDING — /write-be-spec]`; 03.03.02:29 uses `[PENDING — Q-01 / /write-be-spec]`), which shows the correct form was available and applied selectively.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer or a downstream workflow scanning for unresolved product questions treats a `[PENDING — <stage>]` marker as legitimately deferred and moves on. Because the named stage has already completed, no stage ever revisits it — so questions the files themselves label as gating (03.11's event sourcing 'gates the feature'; 03.06.02's density metric, which DT-01 calls 'a product decision, not an analytics one ... because the number is shown') arrive at implementation undecided and get invented by whoever writes the code.

findings.claim: The domain Role Matrix's Fan column and its explanatory note contradict two child specs that grant the Fan full access, and the note states an exhaustive list that is wrong.
findings.evidence: community-networking-index.md Role Matrix — "| 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only |" and "| 03.06-scenes-communities | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only |", plus the note "**Reading the Fan column**: the Fan's access is `Full` only where a feature was built for them (03.02 feed, 03.09 jams/open mics)". CONTRADICTED BY 03.01-connections-follows-endorsements-index.md Role Matrix — "| 03.01.01-follows | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full |" and 03.01.01-follows.md:31 Role Lens — "| Fan | Full | The **only** graph edge available to them (D-02 on the parent)... the follow is the promise that they will be told when that artist does something actionable near them — which is the Fan's entire success criterion"; and by 03.06-scenes-communities-index.md — "| 03.06.01-scene-definition-membership | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full |" with 03.06.01:33 Role Lens — "| Fan | Full (geo only) | Per D-03 they are members of **geo** scenes". community-networking-cx.md CX-09 reinforces the child position: "**Fan**: their follows are the majority of all edges by volume... the alert path (D-11) is their entire product."
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream stage that reads the domain Role Matrix as the authority on persona access — the natural reading, since it is the domain's key file — gates the Fan to read-only on follows and on scene membership. The Fan can then no longer create a follow edge, which removes the carrier of the gig-alert path that D-11 and 03.02.02 D-04 make the Fan persona's entire stated value, and cannot join their city's geo scene, which 03.06.01 D-03 grants them explicitly. The note's parenthetical exhaustive list ('only... 03.02 feed, 03.09 jams') makes the error look deliberate rather than a roll-up artefact.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Fan may create a follow edge and join a geo scene.

findings.claim: The domain index's Children table disagrees with 03.09's own declared status, and the note immediately above the table contradicts the table itself on every row.

findings.claim: 03.10's rights-exposure edge case carries a bare `[PENDING]` with no owner and no deferral target, and its scenario (a host playing a third party's unreleased work) is not the scenario Q-01 tracks.
findings.evidence: 03.10-peer-scene-listening-rooms.md:54 — "| Host plays someone else's unreleased work | Rights exposure via a social feature | `[PENDING]` |". The file's Q-01 (:97) asks a different question — "**What is the platform's position on unreleased material played in social rooms (DT-01)?** Does a room persist as a recording; who owns it; does playing to 30 peers matter to domain 09/12?" — which DT-01 frames throughout around the host's own material ("the entire point of a peer listening session is playing work that is **not released**", "who owns a recording of someone else's unreleased work plus five people's spoken reactions"). No row anywhere in the file assigns an owner or a stage to the third-party-material case.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building room admission or playback must decide whether the platform blocks, warns, or ignores a host streaming material they do not own — the exact act personas.md names as the Musician's worst accidental behaviour ('exposes every collaborator downstream'). With no owner and no stage, the decision is made in code: block and legitimate co-writer playback breaks; ignore and the platform hosts unlicensed distribution of third-party unreleased masters in the domain (09) it claims authority over.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the platform restricts, warns on, or permits a host playing third-party unreleased material in a scene room.

(CX-01 synthesis 1 states it as a requirement: "suppressing a source type should stop the fan-out, not merely filter at render — otherwise the system pays the full cost of delivering content it knows will be hidden"). CONTRADICTED BY the same file :105 — "| Q-04 | Does a suppression control stop fan-out or filter at render? Pick 7 days and a call for a vocalist on a record that takes two months to reach that stage dies before anyone responds; pick 90 days and the market fills with the exact ghosts D-03 names, which 03.03.03 DT-01 establishes kills the demand side's trust after two dead leads. findings.claim: 03.08.02's withdrawal-during-judging edge case carries a bare `[PENDING]` with no owner and no deferral target, and none of the file's three Open Questions covers it.
findings.evidence: 03.08.02-submissions-eligibility.md:57 — "| Entrant withdraws after judging starts | Judges have already spent time; other entrants may be affected | `[PENDING]` |". The file's Open Questions (:103-105) are Q-01 (does a contest result generate a credit), Q-02 (should established professionals be excluded), Q-03 (sample-clearance position) — none touches withdrawal. 03.08-...-cx.md CX-03 synthesis 5 names the scenario but assigns it nowhere: "A submission withdrawn during judging; a submission disqualified after votes are cast." Contrast the same file's sibling 03.08.03:113, where the equivalent bare marker WAS re-pointed with an owner and a stage: "| Q-04 | What is the fallback when a judge goes silent?... | Agent | `/write-architecture-spec` |".
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must decide whether a mid-judging withdrawal removes the entry from the judged set (invalidating scores judges already cast and potentially changing the winner), locks the entry as un-withdrawable (trapping an entrant who has discovered their submission contains an uncleared sample), or withdraws it from ranking while retaining the rights licence the brief froze. The three choices differ in who owns the withdrawn work afterwards — which is exactly what 03.08.04 D-05 ('losing entries revert entirely') has no rule for, since a withdrawn entry neither wins nor loses.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an entrant may withdraw after judging starts, and what happens to their entry's scores and rights position.

findings.claim: 03.06.03's steward-lapse behaviour is an untracked bare `[PENDING]` appearing both as a named state and as an edge case, with no owner and no deferral target.
findings.evidence: 03.06.03-scene-stewardship-moderation.md:74 States — "| Lapsed | Steward inactive | `[PENDING]` — reverts to unclaimed |" and :62 edge case — "| Steward abandons the role | Per personas.md, likely — they have paid work to do. An abandoned steward holds authority nobody can exercise | `[PENDING]` — needs lapse/rotation |". The file's Role Lens for the Producer (:24) states the same expectation as a near-certainty — "a steward role demanding regular attention will be abandoned, and an abandoned steward is worse than none (they hold authority nobody can use)" — yet none of Q-01–Q-04 (:107-110) asks what triggers lapse or what rotation looks like.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must invent the inactivity threshold that trips Lapsed and what 'reverts to unclaimed' does to the steward's prior actions. Choose 30 days and a working musician who tours for six weeks loses their city's scene to whoever claims it next; choose 12 months and the abandoned-steward state the file predicts as the likely outcome persists for a year, holding authority nobody exercises. Nothing in the tree owns the number or the transition.
findings.forcedInvention: The steward inactivity threshold and the lapse/rotation transition.

findings.claim: 03.04.01 D-11 states unconditionally that edges are never deleted, while two edge cases in the same file specify permanent removal — the decision's justification is scoped to age-decay but its wording is absolute and is restated absolutely in the Behavior section.
findings.evidence: 03.04.01-collaboration-graph-path-finding.md:233 D-11 — "**Edges never decay and are never deleted.** Age is disclosed, never weighted" and :80-82 Behavior — "**Edges never decay and are never deleted** (D-11). The fact is permanent — deleting evidenced history is the reconstruction failure run in reverse." CONTRADICTED BY :147 — "| **Dispute resolved against the claimant** | The fact was never true | Edge removed permanently. Any intro in flight that cited it fails closed..." and :162 — "| **GDPR erasure** (`constraints.md` — DSAR unresolved) | Erasure must remove the human from the graph immediately | Node and edges non-traversable at once."
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer building the dispute-resolution cascade reads D-11 in the Decisions table (the section a downstream spec writer treats as the ratified list) and implements adverse dispute resolution as a permanent suspension flag rather than a delete, on the reasoning that 'the fact is permanent'. The false edge then survives in storage and in any consumer that reads adjacency without re-checking suspension state — while a second implementer reading the edge case hard-deletes it. The two builds differ on whether a fabricated collaboration is recoverable, in the one feature whose stated value is that it never carries an unevidenced edge.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether an edge invalidated by dispute is deleted or permanently suspended.

findings.claim: 03.07's Behavior section presents the reputation question as unresolved and cites DT-01 as its source, while DT-01 is marked ❌ REJECTED and D-01 records the resulting decision.
findings.evidence: 03.07-forums-craft-qa.md:36-37 — "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — voting mechanics, accepted-answer semantics, and whether any reputation abstraction exists at all (DT-01) are unresolved." CONTRADICTED BY the same file :72 DT-01 — "❌ REJECTED: reputation-by-participation measures **who posts most**... WeJammin already holds a better credential that cannot be farmed by posting: the credit graph. Displaying evidenced credentials per-craft is strictly more informative than a karma number" and :90 D-01 — "| D-01 | No participation-based reputation system | DT-01 — it measures who posts, not who knows; the credit graph is a better, unfarmable credential. |". The Happy Path (:44) also asserts a mechanic the same Behavior paragraph calls unresolved: "Asker marks an accepted answer; the thread persists as a searchable artefact".
findings.failure_scenario: A reader auditing which questions in this feature remain open takes the Behavior paragraph at face value and reopens the reputation question, or a spec writer treats 'whether any reputation abstraction exists at all' as live and designs one — reintroducing exactly the participation metric that the domain-level law (community-networking-cx.md, 'Evidence beats participation', found independently four times) exists to exclude. The Happy Path's accepted-answer step and the Behavior paragraph's 'accepted-answer semantics are unresolved' likewise give opposite signals about whether that mechanic is decided.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a reputation abstraction and accepted-answer semantics are decided or open.

findings.claim: The 03.06 CX file still presents claiming as the live candidate route to stewardship, which 03.06.04 D-14 and the parent's own Q-04 record as foreclosed.
findings.evidence: 03.06-scenes-communities-cx.md CX-04 map row — "Claiming a seeded scene is how it acquires its first steward — the handover from platform-generated to community-owned" and :84-88 CX-04 detail — "`[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — claiming is one candidate answer to \"who steward-appoints\" (parent Q-04): the first credible local to claim the seeded scene becomes its steward." CONTRADICTED BY 03.06-scenes-communities-index.md:76 Q-04 — "Claiming was the candidate answer (`#CX-04`) and is now foreclosed — 03.06.04 D-14 scopes claiming to **records, not governance** — so no route remains and none of the later stages will choose one", 03.06.04:226 D-14, 03.06.01:196 DT-10 — "an Operator who claims their venue (03.06.04) gains authority over the **venue record**, and remains an ordinary member of the **scene**", and community-networking-cx.md CX-11 synthesis 3 — "claiming a seeded *venue* confers authority over the venue record ONLY, never over the scene".
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer designing the claim flow reads the sub-domain CX file — whose declared scope is precisely the interaction between seeding/claiming and stewardship — and wires scene stewardship onto the venue claim, so the first Operator to claim a room in Bristol acquires governance over the Bristol scene. That is the exact outcome 03.06.01 DT-10 says must be impossible 'by construction rather than by policy' and that CX-01 synthesis 3 states as 'the first person to join Bristol must not own Bristol'.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether claiming a seeded record confers scene stewardship.

findings.claim: 03.01.02 decides that pending connection requests expire but leaves the expiry period as a bare `[PENDING]` that its Q-01 does not cover.
findings.evidence: 03.01.02-professional-connections.md:71 — "| Request is ignored indefinitely | Pending requests accumulate on the target and become a guilt backlog | Requests expire — `[PENDING]` on the period. Expiry is preferable to an unbounded queue the Producer will simply stop opening |". Expiry is load-bearing in the Behavior section (:48-50: "unanswered inbound requests **expire** rather than accumulating an unbounded pending queue") and in DT-05 (:98: "the mechanism therefore needs three cooperating parts — a quota, a same-pair re-send cooldown, and inbound expiry — not one"). Q-01 (:121) asks only about the cap's shape — "What is the inbound throttle model — periodic quota, graph-distance tiering, or a costed request?" — and the sibling parameter in the same table was routed properly at :77 ("`[PENDING — Step 5 Must-depth or /write-be-spec]` on the exact cooldown").
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer must invent the pending-request TTL. Set it to 7 days and a Producer who is mid-album loses legitimate approaches from people they would have accepted; set it to 90 days and the guilt backlog DT-05 identifies as the mechanism's third necessary part does not actually drain, so the Producer stops opening the queue — the failure the whole three-layer control exists to prevent. The adjacent cooldown parameter in the same table was given a stage; this one was not.
findings.forcedInvention: The expiry period for an unanswered inbound connection request.

findings.claim: 03.06.04 sends an abandoned claimed record back to the Unclaimed state while its fields remain operator-authored, but the Unclaimed state is defined as carrying the derived/unclaimed marker — leaving the record's honesty label undefined in the one domain that treats that label as load-bearing.
findings.evidence: 03.06.04-scene-seeding-claiming-cold-start.md:149 — "| **Claimed record abandoned — Operator deletes their account** | The room still exists; the claim does not | Record reverts to **Unclaimed** and becomes re-claimable. It does **not** revert to seed-written (D-08 is permanent for that record's derived fields) — the claimant's last corrections persist as the record's state, attributed to a deleted author...". The Unclaimed state it reverts into is defined at :164 as "| Seeded / Unclaimed | Corroborated (D-06) and published | Record with a visible **derived / unclaimed** marker, its source basis, and a claim entry point." D-02 (:214) requires "Seed records are visibly derived and visibly unclaimed", and DT-03 (:182) makes the distinction absolute: "a derived record is an *inference*, and a claimed one is an *assertion by the responsible party*. Presenting them identically means the platform is vouching for facts it guessed."
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer reverting the record to Unclaimed renders it with the derived/unclaimed marker and the source basis — but the capacity, specs and access details on it are the departed operator's assertions, not platform inferences, and the cited source basis no longer supports them. The platform then labels a human assertion as its own inference (understating), or, if the implementer keeps the authored presentation instead, shows an unclaimed record as authored (overstating). Both violate the domain law DT-03 is applying, and neither is specified.
findings.forcedInvention: How a record whose claimant deleted their account is labelled — derived, authored-but-unclaimed, or something else.
